raw_response:
*thinking in first person as the farmer...*

Well, this is my 26th year on these 8 mu. Same land my father worked before me. I don't have much schooling — never did go to school really — but I know this land. I know when the wheat needs water just by looking at the leaves in the morning. 

My wife is here with me most days. Our oldest son works at a factory in Handan and sends money home, thank heavens, because 8 mu is not enough to feed six people. My daughter-in-law helps when she's not looking after the little one, and my younger brother in the village comes over at harvest time and I help him too. That's how it works here.

**For the wheat** — I'll plant in October like always. The good seed is the one the village cooperative sells, 买的那种 (the bought kind), not seed I saved. Saving seed gives you weaker wheat, everyone knows that. I put about 10 jin per mu (5 kg) in the ground. 

Before I plow I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 bag, it's about 150 yuan now, getting expensive. Then after the winter, when the wheat greens up in March and starts jointing, I put down about half a bag of urea per mu. That's what my neighbor Lao Wang does too, and his wheat is always good. If I saw the wheat looking pale yellow I might give it a bit more, but usually half a bag is enough. Two bags would be wasteful and we can't afford to waste.

Water — the well is right there, shared with three other households. I pay for the electricity. Wheat needs water at least three times: once before I sow in October if the soil is dry, once at green-up in early spring, and once at jointing. Some years if it's really dry I water at grain filling too, but that costs another 30 yuan per mu for the pumping. I watch the weather.

For weeds I spray herbicide once in early spring, it's only 10-20 yuan per mu. I don't spray much insecticide on wheat — only if I see the aphids getting bad at heading.

**For the maize** — as soon as the wheat combine goes through in June, I have to plant maize within a few days. No time for proper plowing. I use the seed drill that goes directly into the stubble (免耕直播). Hybrid seed, must buy new every year — the 郑单958 or similar, whatever the store has. About 3 jin per mu.

Same fertilizer pattern: one bag of compound at planting, then topdress urea at the big whorl stage (大喇叭口期) in late July. Maybe a little more urea for maize than for wheat because maize eats more. Maize only needs irrigation once or twice — at planting if the ground is dry, and at silking if we get a dry spell in August. If rains are good I don't water at all and save that money.

Herbicide I spray once after planting. Sometimes the corn borer gets bad and I spray insecticide once, maybe 20 yuan per mu.

**Money** — this is always the worry. Everything together costs me maybe 6,000-7,000 yuan for the whole year on both crops. Grain prices have been okay but not great. Without my son's factory money we couldn't keep going. I don't take risks with new varieties or fancy inputs — I do what I know works. 25 years I've done it this way and we've never had a total failure.
